title: Chocolate Banana Oreo Overload Loaf
description: An outrageously moist, chocolate-forward potluck loaf made from doctored chocolate cake mix, Oreo instant pudding, bananas, Greek yogurt, crushed Oreos, and chocolate chips, finished with a warm vanilla glaze and more cookies. Tested as a deeply chocolatey success; the banana is subtle.
cookTime: Until the center tests clean; about 45–65 minutes is a starting estimate
totalTime: About 1–1½ hours plus cooling and glazing
ingredients: 1 standard box (about 375–430 g / 13.25–15.25 oz) Devil’s Food or chocolate cake mix
2½ ripe bananas, mashed (approximately 275–300 g peeled; actual weight not recorded)
1 small box Oreo Cookies 'n Creme instant pudding mix, added dry (full package)
Coarsely broken Oreo cookies, a generous handful or more for the batter (actual amount not recorded)
Chocolate chips, as desired, for the batter (actual amount not recorded)
Glaze: about 120 g (1 cup) powdered sugar
Glaze: about 22–30 mL (1½–2 tablespoons) milk, adjusted to a thick, pourable consistency
Topping: additional broken Oreos and chocolate chips, to taste
steps: Grease two loaf pans. Heat the oven to 350°F (177°C) as a practical starting temperature; the exact temperature used in the original bake was not recorded.
Mash the ripe bananas. In a large bowl combine the chocolate cake mix, dry Oreo pudding mix, bananas, eggs, milk, Greek yogurt, and oil. Mix until evenly combined, avoiding unnecessary overmixing.
Fold in a generous amount of broken Oreo cookies and chocolate chips.
Divide the batter between the two pans, leaving room for the loaves to rise. Do not fill more than about three-quarters full.

Bake until the centers are fully set and a knife inserted into the center comes out without raw batter. Begin checking around 40–45 minutes, then continue as needed depending on loaf depth and pan size.
Whisk powdered sugar with milk, adding the milk gradually to make a thick but pourable glaze.
While the baked loaves are still warm, spoon the glaze over the tops. Scatter additional broken Oreos and chocolate chips over the tacky glaze. Let cool and set before slicing or transporting.
notes:
TESTED V1.0 (November 16, 2026): Two loaves, made with 2½ bananas, Oreo instant pudding, 3 eggs, 1 cup milk, 1 cup Greek yogurt, ½ cup oil, chocolate cake mix, broken Oreos, and chocolate chips, then glazed and topped with more Oreos and chips. Result: excellent, very moist, fudgy/chocolate-forward loaf with a good crumb. Banana flavor was mostly lost against the chocolate and Oreo. Exact Oreo and chocolate-chip amounts, cake-mix brand/size, oven settings, and glaze quantities were not recorded; amounts and baking settings above are practical reconstruction guidance, not verified original measurements.

NEXT EXPERIMENT (UNTESTED V2.0): Increase to 4 ripe bananas, reduce milk from 1 cup to ½ cup (120 mL), and swap BANANA CREAM instant pudding IN PLACE OF the Oreo pudding to bring the banana flavor forward. Keep yogurt, oil, eggs, and mix-ins the same initially; watch batter thickness and bake time. Keep V1.0 intact because it is already a keeper.
